The MILCON-VA bill's $152B discretionary spend shows Congress finally prioritizing veterans over foreign aid bloat. While fully funding healthcare and homelessness programs is non-negotiable, the 51.7% spending surge since 2019 demands scrutiny.

Defense jumped from $654B to $826B - taxpayers deserve proof this funds barracks upgrades and Pacific deterrence, not contractor kickbacks. The China procurement ban in Section ### is critical, but real security comes from auditing every dollar.

Veterans earned this support; now make the VA bureaucracy WORK for them instead of expanding its $325B budget unchecked.

Democrats’ $1.5T funding bill isn’t just reckless—it’s a deliberate sabotage of fiscal sanity. Section 2141 repeals critical anti-fraud safeguards from the Working Families Tax Cut Act, opening the floodgates for $200B in taxpayer-funded healthcare subsidies to flow to illegal immigrants. This isn’t a “technical fix”—it’s a brazen expansion of benefits for those who broke our laws, paid for by citizens already crushed by inflation.

The same bill guts $50B from rural hospitals serving actual Americans while prioritizing foreign nationals. Classic D.C. math: Steal from taxpayers, fund lawlessness, then gaslight anyone who points it out.

Shutdowns happen when one party treats your wallet as their slush fund.

Every detail of this fiscal shell game deserves daylight—see the evidence for yourself: https://t.co/xnSbZTUMhV

Expanding VA access is critical, but let’s not pretend new clinics alone fix systemic rot. The VA’s $300B budget still hemorrhages cash into admin bloat—over 30% of staff aren’t frontline providers. North Alabama’s vets deserve specialty care without driving hours, but will this clinic prioritize hiring clinicians or adding more pencil-pushers?

Track the numbers: If wait times drop and outcomes improve, it’s a win. If not, it’s just another taxpayer-funded building with a VA logo.

Audit every dollar.
